name: PFCP
description: The protocol a control-plane function uses to program a user-plane function. It sets up sessions and installs packet detection, forwarding, QoS enforcement, usage reporting, and buffering rules, and the user plane reports usage and events back. It runs on N4 in 5GC and on Sxa, Sxb, and Sxc in EPC with separated control and user planes.

name: GTPv2-C
fullName: GPRS Tunnelling Protocol version 2, control plane
description: The EPC control protocol for creating, modifying, and deleting sessions and bearers and for moving UE contexts between nodes. MMEs, SGSNs, SGWs, PGWs, and ePDGs use it on S11, S5/S8, S10, S3, S4, S2b, and on N26 toward the AMF.

name: GTPv1-C
fullName: GPRS Tunnelling Protocol version 1, control plane
description: The 2G/3G packet core control protocol that creates and updates PDP contexts between SGSN and GGSN and transfers contexts between SGSNs on Gn and Gp. GTPv2-C replaces it in EPC.

name: GTP-U
description: The tunnelling protocol that carries user packets between RAN nodes and gateways, each tunnel named by a TEID. It runs on S1-U, S5/S8 and S12 in EPC, on N3 and N9 in 5GC, on Iu-PS and Gn in 3G, and between RAN nodes on X2, Xn, and F1-U.

name: GTP'
description: A charging transfer protocol derived from GTP, unrelated to session control. A charging data function sends charging data records over it to a charging gateway function on Ga.

name: PMIPv6
description: A network-based mobility protocol in which a mobile access gateway registers the UE with a local mobility anchor on its behalf. EPC allows it in place of GTP on S5, S8, S2a, and S2b, with the PGW as the anchor.

name: DSMIPv6
description: A host-based mobility protocol in which the UE itself registers with the PGW acting as home agent. EPC uses it on S2c for mobility between 3GPP and non-3GPP access.

name: Diameter
transport: TCP or SCTP port 3868 (TLS or DTLS 5658)
description: The IETF authentication, authorization, and accounting protocol that EPC, IMS, and policy and charging use for subscriber data, authentication, policy, and credit control. Each 3GPP interface defines its own Diameter application with its commands and AVPs.

name: RADIUS
description: The IETF AAA protocol that a PGW, GGSN, or SMF can use toward an external AAA server on SGi, Gi, or N6 to authenticate the user of a PDN connection or PDU session, obtain its IP address, and report accounting.

name: SBI
transport: HTTP/2 over TCP, normally with TLS
description: The 5GC control plane between network functions. Each NF exposes REST services described in OpenAPI, and consumers call them over HTTP/2 with JSON bodies, discovering producers through the NRF and optionally routing through an SCP. N32 between SEPPs carries the same messages between PLMNs.

name: S1AP
description: The control protocol between an eNodeB and the MME. It sets up and releases E-RABs, carries NAS messages, handles paging, handover, and UE context management, and transfers warning and positioning messages.

name: NGAP
description: The control protocol between a 5G access node (gNB, ng-eNB, N3IWF, TNGF, W-AGF) and the AMF. It manages UE contexts and PDU session resources, carries NAS messages, and handles paging, handover, and warning and positioning messages.

name: X2AP
description: The control protocol between eNodeBs, and between an eNodeB and an en-gNB for EN-DC. It prepares and executes handovers, coordinates load and interference, and adds and modifies secondary nodes for dual connectivity.

name: XnAP
description: The control protocol between NG-RAN nodes. It prepares and executes Xn handovers, retrieves UE contexts for RRC resume, manages dual connectivity, and exchanges cell and resource status.

name: F1AP
description: The control protocol between a gNB central unit and its distributed units. The CU uses it to set up cells and UE contexts in the DU and to carry RRC messages that the DU relays over the air.

name: E1AP
description: The control protocol between the control-plane and user-plane parts of a gNB central unit. The CU-CP uses it to set up and modify bearer contexts, PDCP, and SDAP configuration in the CU-UP.

name: RANAP
description: The control protocol between the UTRAN and the 3G core on Iu-CS and Iu-PS. It sets up radio access bearers, carries NAS messages, and handles paging, relocation, and security mode control.

name: NBAP
description: The control protocol between an RNC and its Node Bs on Iub. The RNC uses it to configure cells and set up, reconfigure, and release radio links.

name: RNSAP
description: The control protocol between RNCs on Iur. It sets up radio links through a drift RNC for soft handover and supports serving RNC relocation.

name: BSSAP
description: The GSM signalling protocol between the BSC and the MSC on the A interface. BSSMAP handles call setup, channel assignment, and handover, and DTAP relays NAS messages between the mobile and the MSC.

name: BSSAP+
description: The protocol between the SGSN and the MSC/VLR on Gs. It coordinates combined GPRS and circuit-switched attach and location updates and relays CS paging through the SGSN.

name: BSSGP
transport: Network Service (NS) over Frame Relay or IP
description: The GPRS protocol between the BSS and the SGSN on Gb. It carries LLC frames with user data and GMM/SM signalling, along with flow control, paging, and radio status.

name: SGsAP
description: The protocol between the MME and the MSC/VLR on SGs. It supports combined EPS/IMSI attach, CS fallback paging, and SMS over SGs.

name: SBc-AP
description: The protocol between the cell broadcast centre and the MME on SBc. The CBC uses it to start and stop public warning messages, and the MME reports back the delivery status from eNodeBs.

name: LCS-AP
description: The protocol between the MME and the E-SMLC on SLs. The MME requests a position estimate, and the E-SMLC returns it after running LPP or LPPa positioning through the MME.

name: M3AP
description: The MBMS control protocol between the MME and the MCE on M3. It starts, updates, and stops MBMS sessions for broadcast in E-UTRAN.

name: M2AP
description: The MBMS control protocol between the MCE and eNodeBs on M2. The MCE uses it to schedule MBSFN transmission and to start and stop MBMS sessions in cells.

name: EPS NAS
transport: Inside S1AP and LTE RRC messages
description: The signalling between the UE and the MME for EPS mobility management (attach, tracking area update, authentication, security) and session management (PDN connections and bearers). It travels in RRC over the air and in S1AP between eNodeB and MME.

name: 5GS NAS
transport: Inside NGAP and NR RRC messages, or over IPsec on non-3GPP access
description: The N1 signalling between the UE and the AMF for 5GS mobility management (registration, authentication, security, service request), with session management messages that the AMF relays to the SMF. It travels in RRC and NGAP on 3GPP access and over IPsec through an N3IWF or TNGF on non-3GPP access.

name: LTE RRC
transport: PDCP over the LTE air interface
description: The radio control protocol between the UE and the eNodeB. It sets up connections and radio bearers, configures measurements and handover, broadcasts system information, and carries NAS messages.

name: NR RRC
transport: PDCP over the NR air interface
description: The radio control protocol between the UE and the gNB. It manages connection setup, suspend and resume, radio bearers, measurements, and mobility, and carries NAS messages.

name: IKEv2
description: The key exchange that sets up IPsec security associations. A UE on untrusted non-3GPP access uses it to authenticate with EAP-AKA and build tunnels to the ePDG on SWu or to the N3IWF on NWu.

name: MAP
description: The SS7 application protocol for 2G/3G mobility, subscriber data, authentication, SMS routing, and supplementary services between MSCs, VLRs, HLRs, SGSNs, EIRs, and SMS centres.

name: SIP
transport: UDP, TCP, or TLS port 5060 (5061 for TLS)
description: The IMS session signalling protocol. UEs use it to register and to set up, modify, and release voice, video, and messaging sessions, and IMS functions use it among themselves and toward application servers and other networks.

name: H.248
description: The ITU-T media gateway control protocol. A controller (MSC server, MGCF, MRFC, IBCF, P-CSCF) uses it to create and connect terminations in a media gateway (CS-MGW, IMS-MGW, MRFP, TrGW, IMS-AGW) for each call.

name: SCTP
description: The multi-stream, multi-homed transport that carries the RAN and core application protocols (S1AP, NGAP, X2AP, XnAP, F1AP, E1AP, SGsAP, SBc-AP, LCS-AP) and, optionally, Diameter and SIGTRAN.
